q: Lerman and Iwata (1993) found that, compared to functional analysis, descriptive assessments frequently:
choices: A. Yielded enough evidence to design treatment without functional analysis
B. Isolated the maintaining variable as precisely as a functional analysis
C. Misidentified or entirely failed to detect the maintaining variable
D. Produced functional conclusions equivalent to the analysis

q: The primary limitation of indirect assessment for identifying behavioral function is:
choices: A. It depends on informant recall, which is systematically biased
B. It is valid only for self-injurious and stereotypic behavior
C. It must be conducted only after direct observation is complete
D. It requires administration training that most BCBAs do not hold

q: Noncontingent reinforcement reduces problem behavior through which mechanism?
choices: A. Abolishing the establishing operation for the maintaining reinforcer (MO)
B. Signaling that reinforcement is now available for appropriate behavior (SD)
C. Delivering a mild aversive consequence each time problem behavior occurs
D. Increasing the physical effort required to emit the problem behavior

q: A client continues to engage in a behavior described in a rule even after the described reinforcer is no longer being delivered. This most likely illustrates:
choices: A. Schedule-induced behavior produced by intermittent delivery
B. Behavioral contrast from a change in another component
C. Insensitivity to contingencies typical of rule following
D. Spontaneous recovery after extinction has occurred

q: A phase change line in a single-case graph is placed:
choices: A. Through the midpoint of each condition to mark its median level
B. Directly through the first data point collected in the new condition
C. Only when the change in level reaches statistical significance
D. Between the last point of one condition and the first of the next

q: Programming instruction in a client's home language primarily protects:
choices: A. The funder's documentation and eligibility requirements
B. The analyst's scheduling efficiency across the caseload
C. Acquisition and the family's ability to maintain the skill
D. The family's comfort during sessions rather than skill acquisition

q: During escape extinction, a client begins hitting staff — a behavior absent in baseline. This is best described as:
choices: A. Spontaneous recovery of the previously extinguished response
B. Evidence the escape function was misidentified in assessment
C. Extinction-induced aggression, a predictable elicited effect
D. Behavioral contrast, with responding rising in an untreated setting

q: According to Horner et al. (2005), an evidence-based practice in special education requires a minimum of:
choices: A. Three peer-reviewed publications produced by the same research team
B. Five single-subject studies from at least three research groups
C. Ten replications with experimental control across two research groups
D. One well-controlled randomized trial with 20 participants

q: An adapted alternating treatments design assigns separate, equivalent target sets to each procedure primarily to:
choices: A. Remove the need to counterbalance order or signal conditions
B. Permit a return to baseline phase between alternating conditions
C. Keep learning under one procedure from contaminating the other
D. Cut the number of sessions the comparison requires in half

q: The defining structural feature that distinguishes a discrete trial from a free-operant arrangement is:
choices: A. The collection of trial-by-trial behavioral data records
B. An instructor-paced unit bounded by an intertrial interval
C. The use of a discriminative stimulus to occasion responding
D. The delivery of reinforcement after correct responses

q: The changing criterion design demonstrates experimental control by showing that behavior:
choices: A. Changes stepwise to match each successively adjusted criterion
B. Changes only in the tier where the intervention has been introduced
C. Differs across two rapidly alternated treatment conditions
D. Reverses toward baseline levels when the intervention is withdrawn

q: Progressive time delay as a prompt fading strategy involves:
choices: A. Alternating randomly between prompt levels across trials
B. Gradually increasing the interval between SD and prompt
C. Removing the prompt abruptly once the criterion is met
D. Immediately delivering a full physical prompt on every trial

q: Compliance that collapses as soon as the instruction-giver leaves the room most likely indicates that the behavior:
choices: A. Is contingency-shaped rather than controlled by a stated rule
B. Has come under generalized imitative control of a peer model
C. Was maintained solely by the instruction, not by consequences
D. Has already contacted robust natural reinforcement in that setting

q: Which is a required component of a well-constructed contingency contract?
choices: A. A completed functional analysis appended to the document
B. A clear, observable target behavior and its consequence
C. A written guarantee that the behavior will generalize
D. A formal clinical diagnosis of the signing individual

q: Guttman and Kalish (1956) demonstrated that the stimulus generalization gradient:
choices: A. Peaks at the training stimulus, declining as the test stimulus diverges
B. Appears only for visual dimensions such as the wavelength of light
C. Becomes steeper as more training exemplars are added in acquisition
D. Is flat across the dimension whenever training stimulus intensity is high

q: According to Spooner and Spooner (1984), which chaining procedure is universally superior?
choices: A. Backward chaining, because the terminal reinforcer comes first
B. No procedure has demonstrated superiority across all tasks
C. Total task presentation, because every step is practiced
D. Forward chaining, because training follows the natural order

q: Using 'indiscriminable contingencies' as a generalization strategy involves:
choices: A. Thinning reinforcement so the learner cannot predict its delivery
B. Using the same tangible reinforcer in every generalization setting
C. Running generalization probes without the primary therapist present
D. Reinforcing every correct response to maximize the learning rate

q: A multiple relationship in behavior-analytic practice exists when the behavior analyst:
choices: A. Supervises more than one RBT at the same site
B. Uses more than one intervention with the same client
C. Has more than one client on the caseload at a time
D. Occupies more than one role with the same person

q: Which social media action most directly risks converting a public statement into service delivery?
choices: A. Posting general information about how reinforcement works
B. Listing an accurate BCBA certification number on a profile page
C. Giving an identifiable parent case-specific advice in comments
D. Sharing a summary of a published study on the practice website

q: Baseline data for aggression show a steady downward trend before treatment begins. Introducing the intervention now would primarily:
choices: A. Make later decreases impossible to attribute to treatment
B. Reduce variability in the treatment phase data path
C. Improve the immediacy of effect at the phase change
D. Strengthen the eventual demonstration of experimental control

q: A supervisor gives every supervisee exactly two observation hours per month regardless of skill level. This practice:
choices: A. Confuses equal treatment with equitable access to supervision
B. Violates the BACB minimum supervision hour requirement
C. Removes the need for criterion-referenced evaluation rubrics
D. Ensures equity because every supervisee receives identical time

q: Water deprivation functions as a motivating operation primarily because it:
choices: A. Raises the reinforcing value of water and evokes drinking
B. Establishes water as a discriminative stimulus for approach
C. Punishes non-drinking by producing an aversive state
D. Signals that water is currently available in the environment
